importantNotes: Mark is likely the first Gospel written and was a primary source for Matthew and Luke.
Mark emphasizes what Jesus did more than what He said — action over discourse.
'The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom' (10:45).
Mark was written from Peter's eyewitness testimony — vivid, detailed, fast-paced.
The 'messianic secret' — Jesus repeatedly tells people not to reveal His identity.

chapters.1: John the Baptist; Jesus' baptism and temptation; calling disciples; healings and exorcisms.
chapters.2: Healing the paralytic; calling Levi; questions about fasting and the Sabbath.
chapters.3: Healing on the Sabbath; appointing the twelve; blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.
chapters.4: Parable of the sower, the lamp, the growing seed, the mustard seed; calming the storm.
chapters.5: Healing the demon-possessed man; raising Jairus's daughter; the woman with bleeding.
chapters.6: Rejection at Nazareth; sending out the twelve; John the Baptist's death; feeding 5,000; walking on water.
chapters.7: Clean and unclean; the Syrophoenician woman's faith; healing a deaf man.
chapters.8: Feeding 4,000; the yeast of the Pharisees; Peter's confession; first prediction of death.
chapters.9: The Transfiguration; healing a boy with an evil spirit; who is the greatest?
chapters.10: Teaching on divorce, children, and wealth; the rich man; third prediction; Bartimaeus healed.
chapters.11: The triumphal entry; cursing the fig tree; cleansing the Temple.
chapters.12: Parable of the tenants; taxes to Caesar; the greatest commandment; the widow's offering.
chapters.13: The Olivet Discourse — destruction of the Temple, signs of the end, watchfulness.
chapters.14: The anointing at Bethany; the Last Supper; Gethsemane; arrest; trial before the council.
chapters.15: Jesus before Pilate; crucifixion; death; burial by Joseph of Arimathea.
chapters.16: The resurrection; the women find the empty tomb; Jesus appears to His followers.
